title: Tiered Dedicated Capacity SKUs and Controlled Autoscale Experiments — Q2 Roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Define and ship a set of tiered Dedicated Capacity SKUs (Small, Standard, Pro) with clearly documented autoscale behavior and a controlled pricing experiment. Goal is to give customers simpler procurement options, predictable unit economics, and the ability to opt into autoscale guardrails that limit burst cost while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket scopes the Q2 roadmap slice: SKU definitions, autoscale policy primitives, billing instrumentation, pilot customer selection, and guardrail telemetry and dashboarding.
objectives: Design three SKU profiles (Small / Standard / Pro) with throughput, prewarm windows, and burst budget defined
Implement autoscale policy primitives exposed in Console and API (min/max capacity, burst_budget, cooldowns)
Run a 6-week controlled pricing experiment with 3 pilot customers to validate elasticity, unit cost, and SLO preservation
Ship billing and cost breakdowns per SKU with per-token and prewarm amortization shown in Console

2026-04-30: Pilot data review and go/no-go for general availability
acceptance_criteria: SKU catalog published in Console and API with pricing and capacity guarantees
Autoscale policy fields are supported in API and Console and can be programmatically set
Billing exports include SKU tag, prewarm amortization, and burst credit usage
Pilot customers report latency SLOs within agreed thresholds and cost within experiment bands
Rollout playbook (canary + rollback) documented with playbook runbooks and oncall contacts
risks: Autoscale burst behavior might cause unexpectedly high bills for naive customers — mitigated via default burst_budget conservative values and opt-in UX
Billing reconciliation complexity for prewarm amortization across time windows
Runtime scheduling regressions when mixing SKU pools with existing Dedicated pools — requires scheduler tests
Pilot customers may have workloads that are not representative, skewing experiment results
decisions: Adopt three SKUs instead of a continuous spectrum to reduce decision friction and billing complexity
Default autoscale burst_budget will be 20% of monthly committed capacity; customers must opt up to higher burst budgets
Billing will expose both token-level and pool-level prewarm amortization metrics to aid transparency
